summary: The state is not sealed. Attributes, outputs and stored plans are stored as plain text, and anyone who can read s3://acme-state/estate can read every value.

file.text: The repository has an access list (.pravo/access/readers.txt), but the state is not sealed. It has not been sealed yet, or someone changed its meta.json.

issues.title: The state is not sealed
issues.text: The repository has an access list (.pravo/access/readers.txt), but the state is not sealed. It has not been sealed yet, or someone changed its meta.json.

suggestions.title: Check why the state is not sealed
suggestions.why: The access list names members, so the state was expected to be sealed, and it is not. It has not been sealed yet, or someone who can write to the store changed its meta.json.

steps.text: If you did not mean to seal this state, remove the access list and the recovery file. To seal it: pravo protect init --encrypt

suggestions.title: Seal the state
suggestions.why: Sealing locks attributes, outputs and stored plans so that only the members on the access list can open them. It needs the store at rest, so announce a short freeze.
suggestions.who: each member, then one of them

steps.text: On the machine of each member:
The access list names 3 members. A member who is not listed sends their line, and it is added to .pravo/access/readers.txt.
